'''Viktor Vasilyevich Dilman''', also spelled '''Dil'man''' (Russian: Виктор Васильевич Дильман, born March 11, 1926, in Proskurov (now Khmel’nitskiy), [[Ukrainian SSR]], [[Soviet Union]]) is a Russian scientist performing research for USPolyResearch. He is best known for his work in chemical engineering and hydrodynamics including the approximate methods for solving nonlinear [[differential equation]]s of mass, heat, and momentum transfer;<ref  name="link1">{{cite book |title=Methods of Modeling Equations and Analogies in Chemical Engineering |last=Polyanin |first=AD|author2=Dilman VV  |year=1994 |publisher=CRS Press |location=London |isbn=0-8493-9914-9}}</ref><ref name="link2">{{cite journal|author1=Polyakov YuS |author2=Dil'man VV |title=Approximate Method for Nonlinear Differential and Integrodifferential Equations |journal=AIChE Journal|volume=52|issue=11|pages=3813–3824|year=2006|doi=10.1002/aic.10995}}</ref> mathematical modeling of chemical reactor processes<ref name="link3">{{cite journal|vauthors=Westerterp KR, Dilman VV, Kronberg AE |title=Wave Model for Longitudinal Dispersion: Development of the Model |journal=AIChE Journal|volume=41|issue=9|pages=2013–2028|year=1995|doi=10.1002/aic.690410902}}</ref><ref name="link4">{{cite journal|vauthors=Westerterp KR, Dilman VV, Kronberg AE, Benneker AH |title=Wave Model for Longitudinal Dispersion: Analysis and Application |journal=AIChE Journal|volume=41|issue=9|pages=2029–2039|year=1995|doi=10.1002/aic.690410903}}</ref> and [[catalytic distillation]];<ref name="link5">{{cite journal|author= Dil’man VV, Lotkhov VA, Lipatova AA, Kvashnin SYa, Kulov NN|title=Dynamics of Unsteady-State Catalytic Distillation in a Packed Column with a Varied Length of the Reaction Zone |journal=Theor. Found. Chem. Eng. |volume=37|issue=6|pages=557–567|year=2003|doi=10.1023/B:TFCE.0000007901.15967.e1|s2cid=95149421 }}</ref> heat, mass, and momentum transfer in turbulent flow;<ref name="link6">{{cite journal|author= Dilman VV|title=The Theory of Heat and Mass Transfer in Turbulent Flow|journal=Int. Chem. Eng.|volume=8|issue=1|pages=156–161|year=1968}}</ref> fluid dynamics in granular beds; surface convection (Marangoni instability),<ref name="link7">{{cite journal|vauthors=Skurygin EF, Dilman VV |title=On Marangoni Instability during Desorption Accompanied by Evaporation|journal=J. == Biography ==

Dilman received MS in [[cryogenic engineering]] from the Moscow Institute of Chemical Engineering (1947), PhD in chemical engineering from the All-Union Research Institute of Oxygen Engineering (Moscow, 1953), and DSc in chemical engineering from the Institute of Nitrogen Industry and Organic Synthesis Products (Moscow, 1968). His major job track record includes head of [[ammonia]] synthesis laboratory at the Institute of Nitrogen Industry and Organic Synthesis Products (1965 to 1988); lead researcher at the Kurnakov Institute of General and Inorganic Chemistry, [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (1988 to present); professor at the Moscow Physicotechnical Institute (1981 to present); senior researcher (2005 to present) at USPolyResearch.

== Major scientific achievements ==

Dilman developed several approximate methods for solving complicated mass, heat, and momentum transfer problems;<ref name="link1" /><ref name="link2" />  proposed a wave model for describing the longitudinal dispersion in turbulent flow;<ref name="link3" /><ref name="link4" /> identified the conditions at which the Marangoni effect can occur;<ref name="link7" /><ref name="link8" /> showed that the diffusion evaporation mode in unsteady [[evaporation]] of liquid into gas may lose its stability if the molecular weight of the evaporating liquid is smaller than that of the gas in contact with this liquid.<ref name="link10" /> The total number of published papers and books is more than 300. Currently serves on the Editorial Advisory Board of Theor. Found. Chem. Eng.
